items.title: 22.6.1 Reactions of the -OH Group in Phenols

source_refs.note: Topic 22.6.1 (PDF 95-96); the equations and the phenoxide sketch are summarised in an original figure. The book's 'an ether is produced' is corrected to an ester.

blocks.text: The -OH group of phenol is slightly acidic, so phenol takes part in acid-base reactions.

items: With bases: phenol is only slightly soluble in water because of its large non-polar ring, but it dissolves in alkaline solutions, reacting to give a soluble salt and water: C6H5OH + NaOH -> C6H5O-Na+ + H2O (sodium phenoxide).
With reactive metals: molten phenol reacts vigorously with sodium, another acid-base reaction, giving a soluble salt and hydrogen: 2C6H5OH + 2Na -> 2C6H5O-Na+ + H2.

With acyl chlorides: phenol heated with an acyl chloride in the presence of a base gives an ester. The base deprotonates phenol to the phenoxide ion, a better nucleophile, which attacks the carbonyl carbon: CH3COCl + C6H5OH -> CH3COOC6H5 (phenyl ethanoate) + HCl.
With diazonium ions: this reaction is described in Chapter 24 (Organic Nitrogen Compounds).

blocks.alt: Three panels: phenol + NaOH gives sodium phenoxide + H2O (acid-base); 2 phenol + 2Na gives 2 sodium phenoxide + H2 (molten phenol); ethanoyl chloride + phenol gives phenyl ethanoate + HCl, with a base. A note says the base forms the phenoxide ion, which attacks the C=O carbon.
blocks.caption: Reactions of the -OH group of phenol (original summary of the book's equations).
blocks.long_description: Phenol behaves as a weak acid: it gives up the hydrogen of its -OH group to hydroxide ions or to sodium. With an acyl chloride, the phenoxide oxygen bonds to the carbonyl carbon and chloride is lost, forming an ester.

blocks.title: Ester, not ether
blocks.text: The book says an ether is produced when phenol reacts with an acyl chloride. The product, phenyl ethanoate (CH3COOC6H5), is an ester, as the book's own equation shows.

blocks.prompt: Why does phenol dissolve in sodium hydroxide solution but only slightly in water?
blocks.explanation: In water the large non-polar ring limits solubility; NaOH reacts with the acidic -OH to form the ionic, soluble salt sodium phenoxide.

items: Phenol + NaOH -> sodium phenoxide + water; + Na -> sodium phenoxide + H2.
Phenol + acyl chloride (with base) -> ester (phenyl ethanoate).
